back: Only strong, non-polar C–C and C–H bonds; no polar links for water, acid, alkali or enzymes to attack.
A polymer whose chains break when it absorbs light, usually UV; often contains C=O groups.
A polymer that microorganisms break down into small molecules such as CO₂ and water.
Gives the dicarboxylic acid and the ammonium salt of the diamine (e.g. ClH₃N(CH₂)₆NH₃Cl).
Gives the diol and the carboxylate salt of the diacid (e.g. NaOOC–C₆H₄–COONa).
Non-stick coatings, plumbing tape, bearings: very low friction and very inert.
Rigid: pipes, window frames. Plasticised: cable insulation, flooring. Durable and insulating.
Protective vests and helmets, ropes, tyre reinforcement: very strong for its mass.
Needs UV light, so buried plastic does not degrade; fragments may persist.
